name: Xuge Guo
bio: I am an M.S. student in Mechanical Engineering at Columbia University, focusing on robotics and control. My research spans robot learning, robust manipulation, and perception-guided assistance, with an emphasis on connecting pretrained models to reliable robot execution.

research_experience.title: DynaInterfere-Bench: Robotic Manipulation under Dynamic Interference
research_experience.role: Research collaboration with Dr. Kaichen Zhou (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) and Prof. Fangneng Zhan (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
research_experience.summary: Controlled benchmarking of vision-language-action (VLA) policies, baseline evaluation, and training-free recovery under dynamic interference.
bullets: Co-developed an Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab benchmark with six YAM Ultra2 manipulation tasks, randomized layouts, collision-aware expert planning, and configurable visual occlusion and periodic or reactive obstacles.
Contributed to 2,000 successful demonstrations (800 xArm5; 1,200 Ultra2), including dual-camera capture, image–state–action synchronization checks, separate train/test seeds, and LeRobot exports.
Integrated π0.5 and X-VLA action adapters; contributed to four-epoch, full-parameter X-VLA fine-tuning on four RTX 5090 GPUs, including checkpoint validation and recovery.
Evaluated fine-tuned π0.5 and X-VLA in 400 seed-matched xArm5 trials per model. Baseline success was 83.75% and 99.75%, respectively, under a shared 90-second task-and-return-home protocol.

Integrated Astra and Sol into an RGB-based robot control pipeline with structured Cartesian and gripper commands, inverse kinematics, and execution feedback. Validated bounded motion with Astra and exploratory mug pick-and-place with Sol without task-specific fine-tuning.

Prototyped a model-agnostic, training-free runtime adapter for risk monitoring, braking, avoidance, and trajectory rejoining, with an initial 12-pair on/off study (24 rollouts). Exploring temporal memory and multi-view 3D context for robustness to occlusion.

research_experience.title: Halo Copilot / SmartHat
research_experience.role: Graduate Researcher · Creative Machines Lab, Columbia University · Advised by Prof. Hod Lipson
research_experience.summary: A wearable assembly assistant combining RGB-D perception, spatially aligned projection, and multimodal step assessment.
bullets: Developed a wearable camera–projector system on Jetson Orin Nano with Intel RealSense D435i sensing to provide guidance on physical workspaces.
Combined 13-class YOLO part detection with Lucas–Kanade optical flow and adaptive detection scheduling for continuous localization during assembly.
Implemented depth-plane estimation, calibrated camera-to-projector mapping, and confidence-aware rendering to keep projected guidance aligned as viewpoints change.
Integrated GPT-6.1-sol for multimodal step-completion assessment against an eight-step XML-defined assembly plan; investigating diagnosis of missing or incorrectly installed parts.

research_experience.title: Training-Free Asynchronous Control for World-Action Models
research_experience.summary: Execution-aware inference and asynchronous control for pretrained FastWAM policies.
bullets: Developed training-free asynchronous control extensions combining continuous policy inference, execution-progress-aware action alignment, and hold-aware action stitching.
Implemented multiprocess simulation and inference backends with dedicated GPU allocation, Pipe-based interprocess communication, reduced observation payloads, and per-stage latency profiling.
Conducted RoboTwin baseline and ablation evaluations across 12 manipulation tasks, with 30 rollouts per method (720 total evaluation rollouts).

projects.title: 8-DOF Quadruped Robot
bullets: Designed and built an 8-DOF quadruped using LX-16A smart servos and Raspberry Pi 4B, integrating mechanical design, inverse kinematics, gait generation, embedded actuation, and physical-robot testing.
Developed a MuJoCo simulation and trained locomotion policies with PPO; compared learned control with manually designed gaits and investigated practical sim-to-real transfer issues.

projects.title: Vision-Based Mobile Robot
bullets: Built a two-wheel mobile robot with real-time vision-based target tracking during the MakeCU hackathon.

teaching.title: Teaching Assistant · MECE 4611 Robotics Studio
bullets: Mentor student teams on robot hardware integration, servo systems, Raspberry Pi-based control, mechanical design, and system debugging; hold weekly office hours and support project evaluation.
